name: Voltyne-GC
description: A graphene-based supercapacitor electrode material produced by Apex Nanofabrication using activated three-dimensional graphene foam structures with a functionally graded pore architecture that maximizes electroactive surface area. Voltyne-GC delivers energy densities approaching thin-film lithium systems while retaining the charge-discharge cycle life and power density characteristic of capacitive storage — millions of cycles with negligible degradation. It is supplied as a dry electrode sheet that fabricators laminate with electrolyte separators to build custom energy storage cells.
applications: regenerative braking energy recovery in transit vehicles
pulse power supplies for directed energy weapons
emergency backup power for critical infrastructure nodes
story_hooks: Voltyne-GC cells are being harvested from decommissioned transit vehicles and repurposed into improvised high-power discharge weapons capable of delivering lethal electrical pulses — the technology is spreading faster than anyone anticipated.
A Tier 4 energy broker is quietly cornering the Voltyne-GC supply in the region, and districts dependent on graphene supercapacitor buffer arrays for power stability are starting to feel the squeeze.

An Apex Nanofabrication materials scientist approaches a fixer with stolen production data suggesting Voltyne-GC has an undisclosed failure mode under specific thermal cycling conditions — one that could cause catastrophic simultaneous discharge in grid-scale arrays.
